This topic moves to a cipher with more keys than a grain of sand has atoms, and breaks it just the same, with the simplest tool of [[pe-descriptiva|descriptive statistics]] there is: counting how many times each letter appears.
El análisis de frecuencias es la primera: Frequency analysis is the first technique in history that broke a cipher without knowing the key, and it is still alive in things that have nothing to do with spies: the programs that detect which language a text is written in look at the frequencies of letters and of pairs of letters; those that recognise an author count words; and file compressors, like zip, rest on exactly the same thing, that some letters appear far more often than others, to give them shorter codes, as you saw in [[av-informacion|information theory]].

El primer tratado de criptoanálisis que: The earliest surviving treatise on cryptanalysis is by Al-Kindi, a scholar of ninth-century Baghdad, and it explains the frequency method with an example in Arabic; it was rediscovered in a manuscript in 1987. In Europe the method reappeared in the Renaissance. In 1586 it served to read the enciphered letters of Mary Stuart, Queen of Scots, who was conspiring against Elizabeth I; Walsingham's codebreakers did not only read them: they added a false postscript in the same cipher asking for the conspirators' names. Mary was executed the following year.
